item.title: Great Western earns into McKinlay Copper-Gold Project
item.dc:creator: JC Villarba

item.ns3:encoded:
Great Western Exploration (ASX:GTE) has entered an agreement to earn up to 100% of the McKinlay Copper-Gold and Silver Project in Cloncurry, Queensland.

The company can earn a 51% interest by spending $500,000 on exploration within 12 months, then acquire a further 29% by spending an additional $2 million over 24 months.

Great Western can achieve 100% ownership by paying between $1 million and $2 million in cash or shares.

Located 80km southeast of Cloncurry, McKinlay sits within the Mt Isa Eastern Succession, which hosts major deposits, including Ernest Henry, Eloise, Osborne, and Cannington. The project comprises two tenements covering 180km2.

Great Western has identified multiple Ernest Henry-style iron oxide copper-gold targets, including Deere, Ventura, and Dylans, plus several Cannington-style silver-lead targets in the southern zone.

At Deere, 1990s drilling returned 28m @ 0.78 grams per tonne gold and 632 parts per million (ppm) copper (Cu) from 78m. The company interprets this as the southern edge of a potentially large-scale system, with no drilling within 1km north of the intercept.

The Dylans target returned copper results including 66m @ 514ppm Cu from 50m, incorporating 14m @ 1,130ppm Cu from 72m. No follow-up exploration has occurred since the mid-1990s.

The project benefits from minimal exploration over the past 25 years, despite historical work by BHP (ASX:BHP), Aberfoyle, Ivanhoe Australia, Sandfire Resources (ASX:SFR), and Newmont (ASX:NEM) identifying multiple coincident magnetic and gravity anomalies.

Great Western plans ground gravity surveys at Deere, aircore drilling at Ventura, and reverse circulation drilling at Stellantis and Dylans once permitting is complete.

The agreement requires shareholder approval under ASX Listing Rule 10.1, as Moffat Resources is 50% owned by Managing Director Shane Pike. Independent directors negotiated the transaction, with Pike abstaining from board discussions. A general meeting is scheduled for late September 2026.

Great Western Exploration also holds the Juggernaut copper-gold targets within the Yerrida North Project in Western Australia.

item.ns3:encoded:
Nexus Minerals (ASX:NXM) reports ‘high-grade’ drilling results from the Templar Prospect within its Wallbrook Gold Project in Western Australia.

Final assay results from 22 reverse circulation (RC) holes (1,810m) at Templar returned intercepts including 7m @ 7.53 grams per tonne Au, including 1m @ 41.27g/t Au, within 23m @ 2.39g/t Au from 48m.

Other results include 6m @ 5.63g/t Au, including 1m @ 15.29g/t Au, within 11m @ 3.17g/t Au from 51m, and 3m @ 4.16g/t Au within 8m at 1.83g/t Au from 40m.

The ‘high-grade’ structure extends previous strong intercepts at Templar, including 7m @ 18.68g/t gold, including 2m @ 43.53g/t Au, within 29m @ 5.29g/t Au from 31m, and 1m @ 57.10g/t Au within 12m @ 5.04g/t Au from 39m.

Managing Director Andy Tudor says the results confirm valuable extensions to the shallow, ‘high-grade’ structure.

“These are excellent, high-grade results from the northern Templar component of the Crusader-Templar Deposit. Drilling targeted extensions to a shallow, high-grade structure and the results have confirmed these valuable extensions,” Tudor notes.

“Importantly, this structure remains open to the north, providing ongoing clear mineralisation upside.”

The Crusader-Templar Deposit hosts a mineral resource estimate (MRE) of 5.7 million tonnes @ 1.7g/t Au for 304,000 ounces. The deposit sits within a structural corridor between Northern Star Resources’ (ASX:NST) Carosue Dam and Porphyry gold operations.

Nexus has now reported Assay results for 171 of 196 RC holes, with outstanding results expected by the end of August.

An updated multi-prospect Wallbrook MRE, incorporating Clement, Payns, Branches, and an upgraded Crusader-Templar resource, is targeted for completion by the end of the September quarter.

Nexus Minerals is a Perth-based resource company advancing a diversified portfolio focused on gold, copper, and critical minerals across Western Australia, Victoria, and New South Wales.

item.ns3:encoded:
Metro Mining (ASX:MMI) has increased waste stripping volumes by 140% year-on-year at the Bauxite Hills Mine in Far North Queensland after investing in additional equipment and productivity improvements.

During July, the offshore floating terminal Ikamba was taken offline to replace four large hydraulic cylinders on Crane One. The Ikamba returned to service on 27 July and resumed full-capacity operations on 30 July.

Geared vessels were used during the outage to minimise the impact on shipping operations.

The shipment guidance for 2026 is between 6.6–7.1 million wet metric tonnes (WMT).

This news comes after Metro Mining achieved a record Q2, with a 7% increase in bauxite shipments compared to the same period last year. Around 1.8 million WMT of bauxite was shipped during the quarter, alongside 779,000 WMT in June alone.

The Bauxite Hills Mine is a single operating mine located 95km north of Weipa in western Cape York. The mine covers 825km2 and has an estimated reserve of 77.7 million tonnes and a total resource of 114.4 million tonnes.

Metro Mining is an Australian miner and explorer based in Brisbane, Queensland.
